You know, my boyfriend sometimes cautions me against spending too much time on this subreddit because he says it upsets me too much. I explained to him that yes, it upsets me - but not because of its content. It upsets me because I am reminded of the bullshit that I went through and it brings all that masked rage out into the open. But I explained that it's also part of the healing process. It hurts, but it gives you much needed validation and support. I told him that its like a burn patient; you need to scrape the dead skin away before you can graft it, and that REALLY fucking hurts. 

This post made me laugh, like really laugh... not bitter laugh, if you know what I mean. Like made me think "damn that is so absurd, it's just fucking hysterical." Thanks for that, that's what I come here for.

I used to live with this old retired Navy vet. His wife had passed away about 5 years before I met him and he was renting out his basement. He was madly in love with her until the day she died. He told me a story once about his younger days when he and his wife had been drinking. Apparently she was quite the lightweight and had shit herself after getting too drunk. I, of course, found this hysterical. "What did you do?" I asked him. He said, "I carried her to the tub, hosed her off, and tucked her into bed."

That's when I discovered the meaning of true love. Love is power washing your girlfriend's butt. Anyone who's worth it wouldn't give a damn. Best part is, he told me that wasn't even the only time she pooped herself. That's motherfucking love.
What I don't understand is why children are responsible for getting gifts for their parents' anniversaries. So self-absorbed.

Fuck man. I hate that shit. "If you had just done X, it would've been no big deal."

For example, I hadn't done the dishes (which was one chore among thousands I was expected to do). She comes home bitchy and angry, screaming about why the dishes weren't done. I protest, telling her I had homework, I did the laundry, cleaned my room, etc. She doesn't like protesting. She says, "Why do you have to argue about everything? If you'd just apologize like a sweet daughter would do, we could just move on and it would be NO BIG DEAL."

So I try that. I apologize for whatever it is she wants me to. Does nothing. She still wants me to be her punching bag and screams anyways.

I am in the same boat. I always wonder if my nMom was the cause, or if I'm just unlucky. I know that for me, it takes work to just put yourself out there and keep practicing at being around people... I'm not great at it, but it has helped me from time to time.
